topic: The dynamical programming algorithm for finite-horizon control
description: Understanding the principle of optimality in the context of finite-horizon control problems; Recognizing how the principle of optimality ensures global optimality of the dynamic programming algorithm; No proof of the principle of optimality required
Understanding the problem that PID control aims to solve; Knowing the PID control rule and the rationale behind its structure

topic: The discrete linear quadratic regulator and iterative LQR
description: Formulation of the linear-quadratic problem in a discrete setting; Derivation of the discrete LQR algorithm; Transforming LQR into ILQR by applying linearization
Formulation of the continuous-time control problem; Approximating the problem as a quadratic program through trapezoidal collocation
Understanding fundamental terminology and concepts related to bandits and bandit algorithms introduced in the course

topic: Bellman’s equations and their relationship to reinforcement learning
description: Form of Bellman’s equations and their iterative solution; The policy improvement theorem and its connection to tabular reinforcement learning methods
Definition of eligibility traces and their role in reinforcement learning; Emphasis on the forward/backward view of eligibility traces

Extending tabular Q-learning to function approximation methods (linear approximators); Understanding the cost function, Q-value representation, and the resulting update rules; Recognizing DQN as a solution to issues in applying function approximators to Q-learning
